Subject: Private offer question: 24-mo vs 36-mo term and approval path

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Skyline's procurement team is moving quickly and I need to firm up the internal ask. Two quick items: 1) They want guidance on whether a 24-month private offer or a 36-month one will be easier to get CFO sign-off (we're showing material produce-side savings for longer term). 2) Who needs to be on the approval chain for an AWS private offer that includes co-sell credits? Procurement asked which buyers/execs we should list to avoid rework on the AWS side.

For context: target seat and usage estimates attached; procurement wants a clear buyer approval lane so they can route the PO. Can someone map approvals + recommended term?

Appreciate it — Paul

Attachments: Skyline_usage_estimate.xlsx (referenced)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Paul Dubois <p.dubois@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Nov 2028 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer question: 24-mo vs 36-mo term and approval path

Hi Paul — thanks for the clear ask and the estimate. Short answer up front: 24 months is usually faster for buyer CFO approval at healthcare orgs; 36 months can be approved if the procurement/finance team is comfortable with multi-year capex/opex treatment and you have an exec sponsor

Recommended approach (practical, reduces approval friction):
- Offer a 24-month private offer with a structured option to extend at pre-agreed pricing (adds minimal procurement lift).
- If Skyline wants deeper unit economics, prepare a 36-month appendix but route that as an internal finance approval path rather than the standard AWS private offer (slower).

AWS-specific approvals for co-sell private offers (what to list):
- Primary buyer (legal/procurement point): name + procurement email
- Finance approver (CFO or delegated finance lead): name + email
- AWS contact (if using Seller Private Offers via AWS): the buyer's AWS account ID and procurement contact so AWS can validate eligibility

I'll loop Vanessa and Marcus to map the internal approval funnel and services/evidence we should attach (SOC2, network diagram, PO template).

Next steps: can you share the buyer legal and CFO contact? We’ll draft a PO template and suggested approval wording you can hand to Skyline procurement.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan

Subject: Re: Private offer question: approval funnel + term split (draft PO + evidence)

Thanks Tessa — drafting here. Paul, adding a practical approval funnel and the minimal evidence pack we recommend for a smooth AWS PO activation: 

Approval funnel (recommended order):
1) Procurement (review PO terms) — routes to
2) Finance lead/CFO (total contract value & payment term approval) — OK to accept 24-mo without exec if <$500k ARR; 36-mo usually requires CFO/executive approval
3) Legal (standard contract review) 
4) AWS activation validation (AWS Seller Support will validate buyer eligibility and apply co-sell entitlements)

Suggested PO wording (short):
- Buyer: Skyline Health (legal entity)
- Term: 24 months (option to extend 12 months at agreed rates)
- Activation instructions: include buyer AWS account ID and procurement contact for AWS Seller Support

Evidence pack (attach to private offer submission):
- SOC2_summary.pdf (one-page)
- network_arch_diagram.png (redacted public-facing topology)
- PO_template.docx (fillable; includes approval fields for Finance & Legal)

Marcus — can you confirm the co-sell credit wording we should include on the PO? Also can you open the AWS seller support case after Paul confirms account ID? I’ll prepare the DocuSign link for the PO once Skyline returns legal contact.

Vanessa
